Arrange your vehicle shuttle before launching.

The GIS name says Musclewood Lake, but its water-trail ID, directions and the DNR river map identify this Kettle River site. The GIS river mile is 46.2; the recommended trip and printed map use 46.3, which governs the published 16.5-mile trip.

areaCenter.feature: DNR public gravel ramp and turnaround area

Kettle River Highway 23 Access (#1).directions: Use the public gravel access north of Highway 23, about 2.5 miles west of Askov. Identify the exit during your shuttle and finish here; Banning State Park’s #2 access is a different site farther downstream.

DNR’s October 23, 2026 construction notice identifies Highway 23 as an available alternative to the closed access inside Banning State Park.

DNR places it on river right facing downstream. Inspect the signed driveway during your shuttle: the inventory says north of the road, while its coordinate and imagery place the access area immediately south of the bridge. The area marker does not locate the exact ramp edge.
Kettle River Highway 48 Access (#5).note: DNR GPS facility coordinate retained unchanged. Satellite imagery shows a riverbank access clearing just south of the Highway 48 bridge; canopy obscures the precise landing. The inventory lists a concrete trailer launch but its north-of-road directions conflict with the coordinate. Keep an approximate area marker and seek a reviewed shoreline correction.

Maple Island Access (#6).sourceName: Minnesota DNR — Kettle River map 2, park map and public access inventory
Maple Island Access (#6).directions: Reach Maple Island through St. Croix State Park using the park road map and posted signs. The park map shows a parking area and carry-in access on the left bank facing downstream. Identify the exit before launching and arrange your shuttle; do not continue into the Lower Kettle rapids to look for another landing. Check seasonal road and park closures.

The 2026 water-trail map calls #6 a trailer access, while the current park map and GIS describe carry-in access. Do not promise trailer access. The trip guide uses river mile 7.9, while GIS says 8.0; use the published 7.2-mile recommended trip. Exact shoreline position remains unresolved.

Straight River Medford City Park Access.directions: Use the public river access in Straight River Park in Medford, off 4th Avenue NW. Follow the signed approach beside the park; check parking and ramp conditions during your shuttle. This is separate from Frank Woodfill Wildlife Refuge farther upstream.
Straight River Medford City Park Access.note: The city confirms canoe/kayak access and the DNR lists a trailer launch. The agency point is at the wooded shoreline beside the approach, without a clear water-edge ramp end. Current DNR map mile 17.1 differs from inventory 17.2.

Straight River Kroghs Landing.sourceName: Minnesota DNR — 2026 Cannon and Straight river map
Straight River Kroghs Landing.directions: Use the signed Kroghs Landing carry-in off County Road 19 south of Faribault. Carry boats from the public turnout to the river. The landing is downstream of the former Walcott Mill Dam rapids; trips arriving from Medford pass those rapids before the take-out.
Straight River Kroghs Landing.note: The agency point is at the bank beside the public turnout. A worn approach is visible, but the exact landing edge is not distinct enough for a precise pin. Retain the original coordinate as an approximate access area.

Straight River Teepee Tonka Park Access.sourceName: City of Faribault — park amenities and canoe landings
Straight River Teepee Tonka Park Access.directions: Use the designated carry-in at Teepee Tonka Park in Faribault and follow the public park paths to the river. Check the landing during your shuttle; the general agency point near the pedestrian bridge does not mark a confirmed water-edge exit. This listing ends before the separate Bridge-to-Park access farther downstream.
Straight River Teepee Tonka Park Access.note: City and DNR sources confirm a canoe landing. The agency point is at a wooded bank near the pedestrian bridge, not a resolved landing approach. The 2026 route table uses mile 2.0; inventory says 1.8. Keep the approximate facility and both source values visible.

Mississippi Kiwanis Park Carry-in.directions: Use the public canoe launch at Kiwanis Park, 1101 East River Road in Brainerd. The city map places the launch on the Mississippi side of the park, separate from the Boom Lake fishing pier. Check the carry approach during your shuttle.
Mississippi Kiwanis Park Carry-in.note: The agency point lies beside the wooded shoreline; the exact carry-in edge is not resolved. The city 2026 park map confirms the canoe launch. DNR route-table mile 1001.2 differs from inventory 1001.1.

Mississippi Riverview Park Carry-in.directions: Use Riverview Park at the end of Riverwood Road in Baxter, reached from Forestview Drive and Scenic River Drive. The DNR lists 6621 Riverwood Road. Follow the public park carry-in approach; inspect the take-out during your shuttle.
Mississippi Riverview Park Carry-in.note: The agency coordinate is beside a wooded approach at the bank. The exact shoreline landing remains obscured; retain the original coordinate as an approximate access area.

Mississippi Crow Wing State Park Carry-i.directions: Enter Crow Wing State Park from State Park Road and identify the designated Mississippi carry-in near river mile 990.4 before launching. This is the downstream carry-in near the Crow Wing confluence, not the separate trailer ramp upstream by the campground. Follow park signs and confirm the parking and carry approach with park staff.
Mississippi Crow Wing State Park Carry-i.note: DNR documents a carry-in near the group-camp area, and the Headwaters Board trip map ends here. The original agency point is at a wooded bank; the exact landing connection remains unresolved.

Mississippi Fort Ripley Landing.operator: Minnesota DNR, Division of Parks and Trails
Mississippi Fort Ripley Landing.directions: Use the signed Fort Ripley Landing off Highway 371 near the Nokasippi River, south of Brainerd. The DNR lists a concrete trailer ramp. Inspect the signed public approach and river conditions while arranging your shuttle.
Mississippi Fort Ripley Landing.note: The agency GPS point is beside the riverfront approach under vegetation, rather than a clearly resolved ramp end. Retain a documented access area, not an invented water-edge coordinate.

Mississippi Fletcher Creek Landing.directions: From County Road 213/Grouse Road south of Camp Ripley, use 210th Street east to the public access entry road. Follow signs to Fletcher Creek landing and check the ramp during your shuttle. This is the DNR-recommended take-out below the Highway 115 bridge.
Mississippi Fletcher Creek Landing.note: DNR lists a concrete trailer ramp. The source point is at a vegetated bank beside the access turnout; the water-edge ramp end is not clear enough for a precise pin.

Mississippi Belle Prairie County Park La.directions: Use Belle Prairie County Park north of Little Falls, reached from Highway 371 and the westbound park entry road. Follow signs to the public river ramp and inspect it during your shuttle.
Mississippi Belle Prairie County Park La.note: The unchanged agency GPS point is on the riverfront approach beside the park clearing. A launch area is visible, but the exact concrete ramp edge is not sufficiently distinct; keep the approximate area.

aliases: Mississippi River, LeBourget Park Public Water Access Site
Mississippi LeBourget Park Landing.sourceName: Minnesota DNR — LeBourget public water access inventory
Mississippi LeBourget Park Landing.directions: Use the public ramp at LeBourget Park, 300 Paul Larson Memorial Drive NW, on the west bank of the Mississippi. This landing is upstream of the Little Falls Dam. Identify it during your shuttle and finish here; do not continue downstream toward the dam.
Mississippi LeBourget Park Landing.note: The unchanged DNR GPS point matches the visible concrete ramp apron at the water edge beside the dock. City May 2026 material confirms this public water access and address. Desktop agency-and-imagery check, not a field survey; the dock replacement proposal does not establish present dock availability.
Mississippi LeBourget Park Landing.bankNote: DNR records R, facing downstream; imagery and the Headwaters Board trip map place the landing on the west bank above Little Falls Dam.

Mississippi Crow Wing State Park Trailer.directions: Enter Crow Wing State Park at 3124 State Park Road and follow signs to the trailer access near the campground. The park map shows it north of the historic town-site area, separate from the downstream carry-in near the Crow Wing River confluence. Inspect the signed ramp and parking while arranging your shuttle; follow current park permit and access rules.
Mississippi Crow Wing State Park Trailer.note: DNR feature WAS02297 documents a concrete trailer ramp at river mile 992.3. Its original digitized coordinate lies on the wooded approach beside the visible ramp, so retain an approximate area. This is distinct from downstream carry-in WAS00990 at mile 990.4. No precise bank badge or water-edge survey is claimed.

aliases: Pine River, Cross Lake Public Water Access Site
Pine River Cross Lake Below-dam Carry-in.sourceName: Minnesota DNR — 2026 Pine River water-trail map and public access inventory
Pine River Cross Lake Below-dam Carry-in.directions: From County Road 3, follow Sand Pointe Drive northwest about 60 yards and the signed approach to the below-dam parking area. Carry to the designated river access below Cross Lake Dam. This is separate from the upstream lake trailer ramp; do not launch above the dam for this trip.
Pine River Cross Lake Below-dam Carry-in.note: The original DNR point identifies the below-dam access area. Trees and snow obscure the exact landing; retain an Area marker. The map labels the broader recreation facility left-bank, while the inventory locates this below-dam carry-in on the west/right bank; no verified bank badge assigned.

Pine River Staircase Carry-in.directions: Use the signed Staircase carry-in about one mile south of Crosslake on County Road 37. Follow the public carry path to the river. If taking out here, identify the landing during your shuttle: Gould Rapids begin shortly downstream at mile 18.4.
Pine River Staircase Carry-in.note: DNR confirms a natural carry-in at river mile 18.5. The original point sits by the wooded bank and approach; the precise stairs and water edge are obscured. Retain the source coordinate as an Area marker.

Pine River Rock Dam Below-rapids Carry-i.sourceName: Minnesota DNR — 2026 Pine River water-trail map and public access inventory
Pine River Rock Dam Below-rapids Carry-i.directions: From Highway 3 south of Crosslake, follow Big Pine Trail east to the signed public access. Carry to the designated launch below all constructed Rock Dam rapids, as directed by DNR. The Area marker locates the facility beside the structure, not the launch point; locate the downstream carry-in before putting in.
Pine River Rock Dam Below-rapids Carry-i.note: DNR recommends starting below Rock Dam. Its facility coordinate is beside the upper constructed rapids, not a confirmed downstream landing. Preserve it as an approximate facility area and leave the landing connection unmapped. This site has blank water-trail join fields and is included in the source import by stable ID.

aliases: Pine River, Harvey Drake Public Water Access Site
Pine River Harvey Drake Landing.operator: DNR Division of Parks and Trails
Pine River Harvey Drake Landing.sourceName: Minnesota DNR — 2026 Pine River water-trail map and public access inventory
Pine River Harvey Drake Landing.directions: Use the public boat landing beside County Road 11, about four miles west of Highway 6 north of Crosby. Approaching downstream, take out on river right just before the road bridge. Lower Pine Rapids begin downstream of this take-out; identify the ramp during your shuttle.
Pine River Harvey Drake Landing.note: Unchanged DNR GPS coordinate matches the shoreline end of the visible ramp approach immediately upstream of the County Road 11 bridge. DNR lists a concrete trailer launch, and its 2026 map independently places Harvey Drake on river right at mile 0.9. Desktop agency and imagery review, not a field survey; water level and ramp conditions may change.
Pine River Harvey Drake Landing.bankSourceName: Minnesota DNR — Pine River route table and public access inventory
Pine River Harvey Drake Landing.bankNote: The route table places Harvey Drake at mile 0.9 on river right, facing downstream. The access inventory agrees, and imagery places the ramp upstream of the County Road 11 bridge.
